verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: These are my special feasts, the feasts of the LORD, which you must announce as holy gatherings.
You may work for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a day of complete rest and a holy gathering. Do no work at all. Wherever you live, it is a Sabbath for the LORD.
These are the special feasts of the LORD, the holy gatherings you must announce at their set times.
The LORD's Passover begins at sunset on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of that month, the Feast of Bread Without Yeast to the LORD begins. For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
For seven days, offer a gift made by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you come into the land I am giving you, and you gather its harvest, bring the priest a bundle of the first grain you harvest.
He will wave the bundle in front of the LORD so that it will be accepted for you. The priest will wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
On the day you wave the bundle, offer a one-year-old male lamb with nothing wrong with it as a burnt offering to the LORD.
With it, bring a grain offering of about three kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil, a gift made by fire to the LORD with a pleasing smell, and a drink offering of about one litre of wine.
Do not eat any bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that day, when you bring this offering to your God. This is a rule forever for all your families to come, wherever you live.
From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the bundle of grain to be waved, count seven full weeks.
Count fifty days, up to the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then bring a grain offering of new grain to the LORD.
From your homes, bring two loaves of bread to be waved, each made from about three kilograms of fine flour and baked with yeast. They are an offering to the LORD from the first part of your harvest.

With the bread, offer seven one-year-old lambs with nothing wrong with them, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, a gift made by fire with a smell that pleases the LORD.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old male lambs as peace offerings.
The priest will wave the two lambs with the bread from the first harvest in front of the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy to the LORD and will belong to the priest.
On that same day, announce a holy gathering and do no regular work. This is a rule forever for all your families to come, wherever you live.

When you gather the harvest of your land, do not harvest all the way to the edges of your field, and do not pick up the grain that was dropped. Leave it for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: On the first day of the seventh month, have a day of rest, a holy gathering remembered with the blowing of trumpets.
Do no regular work, and offer a gift made by fire to the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses,
"The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement, the day of being made right with God. Have a holy gathering, go without food, and offer a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Do no work at all on that day, because it is the Day of Atonement, when you are made right with the LORD your God.
Anyone who does not go without food on that day must be cut off from his people.
I will destroy from among his people anyone who does any work on that day.
Do no work at all. This is a rule forever for all your families to come, wherever you live.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must go without food. Keep this Sabbath from the evening of the ninth day of the month until the next evening."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, the Feast of Shelters to the LORD begins, and it lasts seven days.
On the first day, have a holy gathering and do no regular work.
For seven days, offer gifts made by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day, have a holy gathering and offer a gift made by fire to the LORD. It is a special gathering, and you must do no regular work.

These are the special feasts of the LORD that you must announce as holy gatherings. At them you bring gifts made by fire to the LORD: burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its own day.
These are added to the LORD's Sabbaths, and to your gifts, all your promised offerings, and all the freely given offerings you bring to the LORD.

So, starting on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the crops of the land, celebrate the feast of the LORD for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day is a day of rest.
On the first day, take the best fruit from the trees, palm branches, leafy branches, and willows from the stream, and celebrate with joy in front of the LORD your God for seven days.
Celebrate it as a feast to the LORD for seven days every year. This is a rule forever for all your families to come. Celebrate it in the seventh month.
Live in shelters for seven days. Everyone born in Israel must live in shelters,
so that your children after you will know that I made the people of Israel live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
So Moses told the people of Israel about the special feasts of the LORD.
